01.r: Joins this scene to what goes before.

02.r: Jesus comes upon the trade already going on in the temple.
02.n: Abbott-Smith: 'to find, with or without previous search'. Nothing here says Jesus was looking for it.

03.r: Where the trade was going on.

05.r: The whole temple area, courts included.
05.n: This study renders ἱερόν 'temple' and keeps 'sanctuary' for ναός, the shrine itself. ἱερόν takes in the whole sacred precinct with its courts, which is why the BSB says 'temple courts'.

06.r: The article turns 'selling' into a description of people: those who were selling.

07.r: Traders offering animals for sale in the temple area.
07.n: Abbott-Smith gives the first sense as 'to exchange or barter', the second 'to sell', and lists this verse under the second, with the things sold as its object.

08.n: Abbott-Smith gives 'an ox, a cow'; the BSB's 'cattle' covers both. That these animals were sold for sacrifice is a reasonable inference from the place; the verse does not say so.

09.r: Adds the next kind of animal.

10.n: Abbott-Smith derives the word from προβαίνω, to go forward. In Homer and Herodotus it meant cattle, especially small cattle, sheep and goats; in the New Testament, as in Attic writers, a sheep.

11.r: Adds the last kind of animal.

13.r: Adds a second group of traders.

14.r: Marks the coin changers as a known group at the temple.

15.r: Men who changed money into small coin.
15.n: Abbott-Smith derives it from κερματίζω, 'to cut small, coin into small money', and records this verse as its only use. It is a different word from κολλυβιστής, the word for money changers in Matthew's and Mark's accounts, so this study renders it 'coin changers' to keep the two apart.

16.r: The coin changers sit at their places of business.
16.n: A present participle: they were sitting there when he came. The BSB adds 'at their tables', which this verse does not mention.
